namesake.note: Counts true chestnuts (Castanea) and horse chestnuts (Aesculus) -- an unrelated genus in the soapberry family that is nonetheless almost always what's meant by 'chestnut tree' around Vancouver.
Counts true cypress (Cupressus), false cypress (Chamaecyparis), Leyland cypress (x Cupressocyparis) and bald cypress (Taxodium).
Balsam fir is specifically Abies balsamea, a species not otherwise planted in Vancouver -- but in BC 'balsam' is used colloquially for firs (Abies) generally, so this counts the whole genus.

Covers western redcedar and other Thuja, true cedars (Cedrus), false cypresses (Chamaecyparis) and incense cedar (Calocedrus) -- what Vancouverites mean by 'cedar' is almost always western redcedar (Thuja plicata), not a true cedar.
Prunus also contains plums, laurels and almonds, so this matches on common name (containing 'cherry') within genus Prunus rather than the whole genus.
Counts true firs (Abies) and Douglas-fir (Pseudotsuga), which despite the name is a different genus.

Matches any common name containing 'laurel' -- cherry laurel and Portuguese laurel (Prunus), bay laurel (Laurus), California bay laurel (Umbellularia). These are botanically unrelated to each other; 'laurel' is a shape-of-leaf name, not a real taxonomic group.
Heather (Calluna vulgaris and Erica species) is a low shrub, not a tree -- it never appears in the City's street tree inventory, so this street has no possible namesake tree.

No Vine Maple (Acer circinatum) grows on Vine St in the current inventory (it does exist elsewhere in the city), so there's no tree on the street that plausibly explains the name -- 'vine' almost certainly isn't a tree reference here.
